title: Minimum Time to Break Locks I
summary: Bob needs to break n locks, each requiring a specific amount of energy as specified in the array strength, where strength[i] is the energy needed to break the i^th lock.
statement: Bob needs to break n locks, each requiring a specific amount of energy as specified in the array strength, where strength[i] is the energy needed to break the i^th lock. The sword starts with 0 energy and increases its energy by a factor x each minute. After breaking a lock, the sword's energy resets to 0, and the factor x increases by a given value k. Determine the minimum time in minutes required for Bob to break all n locks and escape the dungeon.
constraints: strength has 1–8 positive values up to one million; 1 <= k <= 10.
The sword begins with factor one, gains that much energy per minute, and resets energy after each lock.
After each broken lock the factor increases by k; choose the lock order minimizing total minutes.
hints: Only the set of broken locks determines the current energy factor.
Use subset dynamic programming and try every remaining lock as the next choice.
For each mask, compute factor 1+popcount(mask)*k and relax mask plus one lock by its ceiling time.
Every order corresponds to one path through the subset states, so taking the cheapest predecessor finds the best permutation.
editorial: Every order corresponds to one path through the subset states, so taking the cheapest predecessor finds the best permutation.

tests.explanation: Break strengths one, four, then three at factors one, two, and three for four minutes total.
An optimal order spends two, two, then one minute, totaling five.
